title: Research: six-call GF(4) scalar-source connector for all two-source rows
body:
## Result

Adds a charged single-source scalar update `S(j,a): z += a B_j x_j` for `a = w,w^2` over `GF(4)=F2[w]/(w^2+w+1)`. For exactly two read-only sources and the 15 nonzero coefficient rows of `GF(4)^2`, one dirty connector path uses six complete source calls, the minimum possible, and 30 complete target readouts. It restores arbitrary connector dirt and uses no extra helper or source copy.

The six prefix points have all 15 distinct pairwise differences. The lower bound is `binom(k,2) >= 15`, since a closed `k`-event path has at most `k` distinct prefix points. Each target gets two `A_r` readouts at its certified boundary pair; characteristic two cancels the arbitrary dirty connector term.

The complete parametric bill compares this shared path with an explicit per-target schedule under the same added alphabet:

- source map calls: `6` versus `48`;
- nonunit GF(4) scalar work: `4L` versus `32L` bitwise XORs;
- prefix-coded event storage: `174` versus `342` bits.

With `c_Bj` the fully charged unit-coefficient source event price (map child, source access, connector update, dispatch, frame/head travel, and scratch restoration), and `beta` the descriptor-bit price, the saving is `21(c_B0+c_B1) + 28L + 168 beta`; both schedules use the same 30 complete `A_r` calls and common interpreter bill. The full model and literal event stream are in the package. No supplier admission or new `kappa` is claimed.
